newsitem.title: USA: Missouri House Republican leader quits.
newsitem.headline: Missouri House Republican leader quits.

text.p: Missouri House Republican leader Mark Richardson said Tuesday he was stepping down from his post after being charged with drunken driving and child endangerment.
Richardson made his announcement Tuesday after meeting with other Republican legislators.
House Republicans had also met privately Monday night to discuss whether Richardson should remain as minority floor leader, step down or retain the job for the last three weeks of the session.
An election to replace Richardson will be held Monday.
Richardson was arrested Friday by a Missouri Highway Patrol trooper near Jefferson City. Richardson's four-year-old daughter was in the car with him at the time.
Cole County Prosecutor Richard Callahan's office charged Richardson Monday with one misdemeanor count of driving while intoxicated, punishable by up to six months in jail.
Richardson was also charged with a misdemeanor count of endangering the welfare of a child, a charge that is punishable by up to one year in jail.
